ei.title: Interoception and Empathy Through the Body
ei.subject: 수능특강

fullPassage: Becoming aware of our internal sensations can help us handle our own emotions. Perhaps more surprisingly, the body's interoceptive faculty can also bring us into closer contact with other people's emotions. That's because the brain, on its own, has no direct access to the contents of other people's minds, no way to feel what others are feeling. Interpreting others' spoken words and facial expressions may yield only a coolly abstract sense of the emotions that stir within. The body acts as a critical conduit, supplying the brain with the visceral information it lacks. It does so in this way: When interacting with other people, we subtly and unconsciously mimic their facial expressions, gestures, posture, and vocal pitch. Then, via the interoception of our own bodies' signals, we perceive what the other person is feeling because we feel it in ourselves. We bring other people's feelings onboard, and the body is the bridge. In an act similar to taking a bite off our partner's plate, or borrowing an earbud to hear the song our friend is listening to, we are sampling their emotions.

The body acts as a critical (B)[barrier / conduit], supplying the brain with the visceral information it lacks. It does so in this way: When interacting with other people, we subtly and unconsciously mimic their facial expressions, gestures, posture, and vocal pitch. Then, via the interoception of our own bodies' signals, we perceive what the other person is feeling because we feel it in ourselves. We bring other people's feelings onboard, and the body is the (C)[bridge / obstacle]. In an act similar to taking a bite off our partner's plate, or borrowing an earbud to hear the song our friend is listening to, we are sampling their emotions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:

det.analysis: information(명사) 앞 수식어 자리. viscera(명사) → visceral(형용사)로 변환

questions.passage: When interacting with other people, we subtly and _____(1) mimic their facial expressions, gestures, posture, and vocal pitch. Then, via the interoception of our own bodies' signals, we perceive what the other person is feeling because we feel it in ourselves.

다음 글의 빈칸에 주어진 단어의 올바른 형태를 (영어로) 쓰시오.
(1) unconscious (무의식적인)

det.korean: unconscious(형용사) → unconsciously(부사): 동사 mimic을 수식하는 부사 필요
det.analysis: 동사 mimic을 수식하는 부사 자리. unconscious(형용사) → unconsciously(부사)로 변환
det.tip: 동사 수식 = 부사. subtly and _____ mimic → 병렬 부사

questions.passage: Becoming aware of our internal sensations can help us handle our own emotions. Perhaps more surprisingly, the body's interoceptive faculty can also bring us into closer contact with other people's emotions. That's because the brain, on its own, has no direct access to the contents of other people's minds, no way to feel what others are feeling. Interpreting others' spoken words and facial expressions may yield only a coolly abstract sense of the emotions that stir within. The body acts as a critical conduit, supplying the brain with the visceral information it lacks. It does so in this way: When interacting with other people, we subtly and unconsciously mimic their facial expressions, gestures, posture, and vocal pitch. Then, via the interoception of our own bodies' signals, we perceive what the other person is feeling because we feel it in ourselves. We bring other people's feelings onboard, and __________. In an act similar to taking a bite off our partner's plate, or borrowing an earbud to hear the song our friend is listening to, we are sampling their emotions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① the mind is the filter — 본문 논지(몸의 역할)와 무관
❌ ② the brain is the source — 뇌가 감정 원천이라면 본문과 모순
❌ ③ the emotion is the key — 추상적이며 구체적 비유와 불일치
✅ ④ the body is the bridge — 몸이 다리로, 감정 연결의 비유 ←정답
det.tip: the body is the bridge = 몸이 다리
